title: REVOLUTION MEN'S LEAGUE | WEEK 3 RECAP
content: Week 3 delivered fireworks from the opening tip to the final buzzer of the Revolution Men's League. Chris Cayole caught fire for 33 points but couldn't push Red past Blue, Purple ground out a road win over Orange, Tavian Barrino exploded for 46 points to carry Pink past Black, and Gray held off a late Green rally to escape with the win. Let's get into the action.

games.text: Blue came out looking to make a statement early. Blue's balance was the story of the first half, with Drew Pelkey and Brody Lathrop combining to keep the offense humming while Logan Letourneau and Henry Cogswell chipped in from every angle. Red answered behind Chris Cayole, who was already raining threes, but Blue's depth off the bench gave them just enough cushion to head into the break in front. Blue led 49-44 at the break. The second half tipped the other way for a stretch, but Blue's balanced attack proved too much to overcome down the stretch. Red poured everything into the comeback, with Chris Cayole erupting for a game-high 33 points and Will Oboh adding 23 of his own on efficient shooting. Jaren Jeffcoat controlled the glass with 13 boards to keep Red within striking distance, but Red could only match Blue's 36 second-half points, and the first-half deficit was too steep to climb out of. Blue held on for an 85-79 win.

performers.Red: Chris Cayole — 33 pts, 13 REB, 1 AST; Will Oboh — 23 pts, 3 REB, 2 AST; Jaren Jeffcoat — 20 pts, 13 REB, 2 AST
performers.Blue: Brody Lathrop — 21 pts, 5 REB, 2 AST; Drew Pelkey — 21 pts, 9 REB, 3 AST; Logan Letourneau — 12 pts, 6 REB, 5 AST

games.text: Purple refused to let this one slip away. Kevin Garrison set the tone immediately, attacking the rim and knocking down threes to give Purple an early cushion. Orange leaned on Kenny Black and Stefan Radan to battle on the boards, but Purple's balanced scoring from Brody Snow and Dennis Schut kept the margin comfortable heading into halftime. Purple led 29-22 at halftime. Orange tried to claw its way back in the third and fourth quarters, leaning on its size advantage down low. Kenny Black and Stefan Radan combined for 26 points and 26 rebounds in the second-half push, and Will Ewald chipped in on the glass as well, but Orange never fully closed the gap. Purple's second-half offense matched Orange point for point, which was enough to protect the early lead. Purple escaped with a 61-54 win.

performers.Purple: Kevin Garrison — 24 pts, 9 REB, 1 AST; Brody Snow — 15 pts, 9 REB, 2 AST; Dennis Schut — 12 pts, 5 REB
performers.Orange: Kenny Black — 14 pts, 14 REB, 1 AST; Stefan Radan — 12 pts, 12 REB, 2 AST; Will Ewald — 11 pts, 11 REB, 2 AST

games.text: Pink had one thing on its mind: put on a show. Tavian Barrino started scoring in bunches from the opening minutes, getting to his spots at will and knocking down shots from all three levels. Jerrick Jacobs and Matt Riordan added secondary scoring to keep the pressure on, while Black leaned on Tavarius Vance just to stay within range. Pink led 34-27 at the break. Barrino never let off the gas in the second half, turning a comfortable lead into a rout. Tavarius Vance kept fighting for Black, finishing with 27 points and 10 rebounds to keep the scoreboard respectable, and Kaleb Swetty and Liam Walsh both reached double figures. But Barrino closed out an eye-popping 46-point performance, and Pink's offense simply had no answer coming from the other side of the floor. Pink pulled away for an 85-68 win.

performers.Pink: Tavian Barrino — 46 pts, 5 REB, 5 AST; Jerrick Jacobs — 14 pts, 3 REB, 2 AST; Matt Riordan — 10 pts, 7 REB, 2 AST
performers.Black: Tavarius Vance — 27 pts, 10 REB, 2 AST; Kaleb Swetty — 13 pts, 8 REB, 2 AST; Liam Walsh — 13 pts, 5 REB, 1 AST

games.text: Gray needed every possession to survive this one. Gray's frontcourt set the tone early, with Sub Mahlik and John Helsel controlling the glass and Adam Gawrys knocking down outside shots to build a cushion. Green struggled to find its footing offensively in the opening minutes, missing chance after chance despite Aaron West's early scoring. Gray led 33-24 at halftime. Green found its rhythm coming out of the break and made a real push to get back into it. Aaron West carried the load with 19 points on the night, and Wyatt Jarvis-Comi added a strong all-around effort. Green outscored Gray 26-20 in the second half and cut what had been a nine-point deficit down to the wire, but the comeback fell just short. Gray held on for a 53-50 win.

performers.Gray: Adam Gawrys — 15 pts, 4 REB; Sub Mahlik — 14 pts, 14 REB, 5 AST; John Helsel — 12 pts, 12 REB, 3 AST
performers.Green: Aaron West — 19 pts, 7 REB, 2 AST; Wyatt Jarvis-Comi — 10 pts, 6 REB; Paddy Monaghan — 6 pts, 14 REB, 1 AST
